source: current user message choosing in-place CodeGraph preparation against an explicitly dedicated Vulgata-managed prepared workspace
decision: Revise Story 18.3 specification and plan toward in-place CodeGraph preparation/native MCP in a bound dedicated Vulgata-managed prepared workspace; do not create an extra source copy solely because CodeGraph stores its index inside the project.
conditions: Prepared source files remain unchanged and ordinary Worker source tools remain read-only; trusted adapter writes are limited to declared contained tool state, normally .codegraph for pinned CodeGraph 1.5.0.
Root/project selection stays outside model arguments; preserve containment, live authorization, cancellation, owned-process cleanup and safe treatment of pre-existing tool state.
One coordinated owner controls preparation/index mutation with a defined native-session sharing policy; no per-Worker index rebuild or deletion.

Inspect and qualify startup path; avoid optional project configuration edits and Git hook installation, and report any unavoidable writes outside declared tool state before requesting wider authority.

Generated tool state must not become source evidence or silently affect 18.1 source-search traversal/continuations; Vulgata Master is assessing the owning correction scope, so Story 18.3 must not invent a competing source-filtering contract.
Coordinate the smallest bound tool-state-write adjustment through Story 18.2 shared lease owner; its existing read lease is not a write grant.

No Git acquisition, Source Snapshot substitute, repository-wide hashing, automatic source monitoring, source-copying service, retained-source weakening, arbitrary repositories, credentials, databases or provider services.
authority_limit: This user message authorizes revision of affected definition and plan, not skipped review/approval gates, process execution against an unspecified directory, shared-story edits, or resolution of 18.2/file-tool holds.
supersedes: The conditional temporary source-copy recommendation in plan-review-04; historical artifacts/reviews and valid independent implementation evidence remain preserved.
